# A01-S54: Research reference

Correspondence extract. [████] marks redaction; […] marks omission.

[…] 

I have read Conn’s dissertation: “The Body Politic: Socialist Science
Fiction and the Embodied State” (May 2021, 258 pages plus references).
Excellent reading if, like me, you are a sci-fi enthusiast. However, I’m not
sure I would recommend it for full reading among innocent
readers. It is too narrow – and a bit too American in its approach to
”socialism”, which is very different from our European worldview.

[████] might find it more interesting because of the academic approach and
several good analyses of linguistic expression in cultures other than the
Western one. [████] will get a quite special Chinese reference and
comparison to the Japanese Manga. I think you others will find it
somewhat special, because it takes its starting point in a very academic and
intellectual treatment of sci-fi literature, although it can also appear
with a political stance, and as such it is also an excellent
cultural-political analysis for understanding future worldviews connected to today’s
Chinese strategies on technology.

I will not declare it a "must read" – but please do read the conclusion from page
231-258. In other words, it is for nerds, and if it were in book form I would
have made the title a bit sexier and for example called it – *New Humans: A
Communist Doctrine For The Future*. I discovered a couple of gaps in my knowledge
of sci fi, which I didn't know I had; that's how it is when you "primarily" 
read Western literature. As a dissertation on sci fi it is therefore
interesting. Not because the "stories" analyzed there are so much different
in content/context than the Western future scenarios. I don't know if I
agree with her in all her analyses, but there are definitely a couple of books that
I personally would like to read on her recommendation.

Conn’s exposition of the "body and mind" arguments is in my opinion
not explicitly socialist/communist applicable. Conn’s completely
the overall approach could "in Danish" very well be expressed as an analysis of
[…] Humans being freed from labor in all eternity” *or* ”Eliminating
human labor through technology”. In fact, I want to make a completely different connection
to the current western #MeToo waves and ask all women with connections
hereto about reading the thesis with regard to the *main theme* about work
(labor = the doctrine of Marxism and view on women) … i.e. dissolve the family as
core unit, eliminate the mother role – and get started on obtaining
produced the sex robots. *What the…?*

Well, that was the *teaser* J. Chapter 1 and 2 follow the academic norm,
[████] This is thus not a review to be used
for MF, [████]
we can also just discuss robots and genetic manipulation for
future humans, who could end up without work – that is a
societal model where work is not necessary and where a system other than
capitalism is introduced – e.g. basic income etc.?
